text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Moslem-Croat federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic says in interview salaries for state employees will remain frozen for six months to allow for closer regulation of the state budget. Overdue wages for cultural and scientific workers will be paid this week, he said.
- Bicakcic says customs laws should be reviewed and says state will reconsider subsidies for some cultural institutions.
- Nine empty houses in village of Memici in Bosnian Serb territory were blown up early on Sunday, NATO-led Stabilisation Force said. The houses were formerly inhabited by Moslems.

- The coalition for return, an organisation trying to help bring Bosnian refugees back to their homes, plans to open regional offices in several towns across the country, the coalition agreed at a meeting in Tuzla.

- Levelling charges against Bosnian Moslem leaders from the divided town of Mostar fuels tensions inside Bosnia's Moslem- Croat Federation and signifies death knell of Croat self-styled state, commentary says.

- European Union council of ministers expected to support proposal of international envoy to Bosnia Carl Bildt on reinforcing international police presence in the disputed town of Brcko with 200 monitors.
